The user wants me to push beyond basic sharding to really cut down on lock contention in the cache. The key insight is that strict LRU forces write locks on every read just to update recency information, which is the bottleneck. I'm exploring solutions like using lock-free read buffers to batch access updates, so reads don't need to acquire locks immediately. Defining the node structure... Right, the read buffer solves this — reads don't mutate the LRU at all, they just check if the entry is expired and return None if so, then push to the lock-free queue for later promotion. The actual removal happens asynchronously via the janitor or on the next write. I'm sketching out the shard structure with cache-line padding, an RwLock for the inner state, and an ArrayQueue for the read buffer to hold slab indices with generation numbers.

Defining the get method... I'm deciding whether to store keys in both the map and nodes or use Arc<K> to avoid duplication—the tradeoff between simplicity and memory efficiency. For now I'll keep it straightforward with K stored in both places and require Clone, since that's cleaner than trying to manage a single source of truth. On the buffer side, I'm thinking about when to drain it: draining on every write is simpler than tracking a high water mark, and even if reads vastly outpace writes, occasional buffer drops are acceptable since the LRU is already approximate anyway.

Writing the full implementation... Implementing the insert method to handle key updates with generation tracking and TTL support, then evicting LRU entries when capacity is reached before adding new nodes to the front of the list.

Now I'm setting up the Shard wrapper with read/write locking, a read buffer for deferred touch operations, and atomic counters for cache hits and misses. The get method checks expiration, records statistics, and attempts to defer the LRU touch to the read buffer to avoid write lock contention. Writing cache initialization... Finishing the janitor thread logic and wrapping up the cache implementation with statistics tracking. Now I need to lay out the full ShardInner methods that handle the core operations like detaching and touching entries, then organize the response to explain why the original design still has contention issues and walk through three concrete optimizations with their performance tradeoffs.
